html:
SMTO-SCH-0015 — SMTO couldn't apply that schedule change

GUID: 6438b957-ab14-4b8b-abc9-c0b56f2c0dd9
Slug: schedule-edit-invalid
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • The request to look at or change a schedule was missing something or asked for a change SMTO doesn't allow, such as an edit with nothing in it. The schedule was not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Schedules, select Edit on the schedule you mean, change at least one field, and save. SMTO rejects an edit that has no actual changes or leaves a field empty.
  2. To stop a schedule, use Pause, Cancel schedule (in the ⋯ menu) or Delete instead of asking for a different status. Stopping and removing a schedule have their own buttons; an edit can only switch between running and paused.
  3. If you asked the Agent, tell it the exact schedule name and what to change, for example "move Daily report to 8:00 AM". Showing a schedule's details or changing it needs one specific schedule, not the whole list.

What success looks like

  • The schedule's card on the Schedules page shows your change, and no error appears.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO with a note of the change you wanted. Don't keep sending the same request unchanged; it will be rejected the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A schedule inspection or edit request was rejected: details were requested without a schedule ID, the edit was empty or set a field to null, or it requested a status other than active/paused.

What this means

  • Schedule inspection lacks an ID for detailed fields, or editing is empty, requests unsupported status/null fields or applies a summary option to the wrong action/type. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Schedule inspection lacks an ID for detailed fields, or editing is empty, requests unsupported status/null fields or applies a summary option to the wrong action/type.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish missing detail-selection identity from invalid update fields and action-specific summary options.

How to fix it

  • Check the request against ScheduleManagementService.inspect/update: include_instruction or include_runs require a single schedule_id; an update must contain at least one field, no field except recurrence may be null, and native status edits accept only active or paused (use the cancel or delete operations instead). Correct the named field and resubmit for the intended schedule ID.
  • Select an exact schedule for detailed inspection and correct edit fields against the current operation schema.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported inspect/edit request applies only to the intended current schedule.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
